Includes the intervening agent door and relay, support channels and consent, voice, mobile notices, knowledge publication and entitlement boundaries, procedures, follow-ups and personal Slack/Teams notices. Pins rer 0.2.102. migrations.buyerSteps: Apply before the updated Worker serves traffic. Adds quoted follow-up proposals and human-accepted responsibility history; no customer message is sent automatically. Erasing a customer purges their obligations.

Apply before the updated Worker serves traffic. Adds immutable advice-procedure versions, exact-version evaluation release gates and bounded explicit cohorts. No business-action tools are added. A stopped cohort stays with a human review requirement until explicitly enrolled into another approved release; historical evaluations and version links remain available.

Apply before the updated Worker serves traffic. Adds reviewed, source-linked private knowledge proposals and corrective review records. No draft is automatically published; named editors confirm redaction review. Source-derived publication is held to the customer’s currently proven email-domain collection. Erasing that source customer removes the derived articles and proposals.

Apply before serving the updated Worker. A native reopening of a cycle answered by an active advice procedure now stops that exact bounded rollout automatically, cancels its queued/running generations and restores an active human owner without publishing an AI draft. A lead must explicitly enroll an approved release and hand the conversation back to AI to resume; existing cases, reviews and failures remain retained.

Apply before the updated Worker serves traffic. Gives reviewed translations their own publication identity, preserving existing drafts and reviewed text. AI retrieval and admission now fence the exact translated publication and disclose source-language fallback.

Apply before serving the updated Worker. Lets knowledge publishers select one exact help host already mapped to their workspace by PUBLIC_HELP_HOSTS, or select built-in paths. DNS and TLS remain the hosting administrator’s prerequisite; existing mapped hosts keep working until a lead makes a choice.

Apply before the updated Worker serves traffic. Records allowlisted per-tool timing, scoped read/proposal authority, denial and human handoff metadata. No arguments, response text, credentials or external business-action authority are added. Started calls without a terminal receipt remain unknown.

Apply before serving the updated Worker. Adds append-only human attribution corrections backed by an exact native message. Reports show original cycle counts, corrected denominators and retained reviews separately. Corrections do not resume a stopped rollout or convert a closure into verified recovery.
Create the shared MCP credential, policy, approval, audit, replay and event stores before serving the agent door. Existing support records and sessions are preserved.
Create signed Business settings storage after migration 277. No company policy is presumed or adopted by this migration.
Add durable Business person-id mappings after migration 278. Existing native people retain their native roles; token email never selects an account.

Link an unambiguous existing native owner workspace and retain separate agent/sponsor attribution after migration 279. Ambiguous installations require an explicit owner workspace choice. No customer message is sent.

Apply after 290 and before the updated Worker serves traffic. Add nullable stored ticket-group scope to custom roles. Existing roles retain NULL and keep their prior authority; no activating backfill or public scope controls are introduced. Preserve role selections with the existing project_roles data during backup and restore.

Back up D1, R2, Durable Objects and private settings, then apply once after 297 and before serving the 0.2.96 agent door. Add the installation-private relay and replay-alias stores, agent tombstones and the fixed 30-day call replay expiry; completed legacy calls expire from their original created_at, never upgrade time. Backfill only consented MCP audits under the current Business envelope; older pairing authority is not reconstructed. Preserve native owners, support records, audit retention and all applied migration identities. Relay and replay aliases never travel in portable archives. No provider configuration, production change or outbound relay is enabled.

Back up D1 first; apply once after 302_move_in_zendesk_pull.sql, before serving the updated Worker. Adds only personal Teams consent, session-bound single-use link codes, verified personal conversations, preferences and outcomes. Off by default; no backfill or replay. All five tables are excluded from exports; reconnect and link explicitly after restore.

Back up D1 first; apply once after 303_teammate_teams.sql, before serving the updated Worker. Adds one small table recording which articles the Article import page's Intercom and Freshdesk import wrote, so a workspace whose published help is only imported is served with noindex until a member publishes. No backfill or replay: earlier API imports keep today's behaviour, and Move in and legacy imports are covered from their existing records. It holds no personal data and travels with exports.

Back up D1 first; apply once after 304_knowledge_import_origins.sql, before serving the updated Worker. Adds one table of hashed one-time Mailgun signature tokens and their receipt times, used only to refuse a replayed Mailgun route forward. No personal data, no backfill, no effect until MAILGUN_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_KEY is set. The table is pruned by email maintenance and excluded from exports.

Back up D1 first; apply once after 305_mailgun_inbound_tokens.sql, before serving the updated Worker. Additive only: one cutover_steps table for the steps an owner or admin records in Settings > Cutover, and five indexes that keep that page's live counts off full scans (conversations, Move in conversations, legacy import rows and inbound email). No backfill, no existing row changes, nothing is sent, queued or enabled. The table travels in exports with the rest of D1.

Back up D1 first; apply once after 306_cutover_steps.sql, before serving the updated Worker. MIGRATION-001 legacy delta sweeps: adds legacy-import bookkeeping only (import state per imported row, delta conflicts, a transient batch mark table); a delta finds journal rows by source row through the index 306_cutover_steps.sql adds. No business table, trigger or row changes and nothing runs. An installation imported from legacy before this migration replays its original package once with the existing import command before its first delta sweep; that exact replay changes no business row or file.

Back up D1 first; apply once after 307_legacy_import_delta.sql, before serving the updated Worker. Additive only: a receipts table with one row per object the optional Amazon SES S3 reader lists (and an index of the few that still hold a private copy), and a one-row table of its last list. No backfill, no existing row changes, nothing is read, sent, queued or enabled: the reader stays off until LEGACY_MAIL_S3_BUCKET, LEGACY_MAIL_S3_PREFIX, LEGACY_MAIL_S3_MAILBOX, LEGACY_AWS_REGION, LEGACY_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and LEGACY_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY are all set. The receipts travel in exports with the sender address and private copy reference cleared; the list state stays with the installation.

Back up D1 and R2 first. Apply once after 308_legacy_mail_s3.sql and before serving the updated Worker. Adds the Zendesk attachment-file runs, a per-workspace ledger of each imported comment's attachments by Zendesk id (ids, states and reason codes only; no file name, URL or token), the tickets Zendesk no longer returned, and links from imported private notes to their files. Existing imports, media and private notes are unchanged; no run starts by migration, and files are fetched only when an owner or admin chooses Fetch files over the existing Zendesk connection. Fetched files live in R2 under import-bytes/ with their media rows; back up and restore them with the native media.

Back up D1 first; apply once after 309_move_in_zendesk_attachments.sql and before serving the updated Worker. Adds a derived contact-identity view and secure-delete trigram search index, its initial rebuild and maintenance triggers, plus an index on imported conversation source ids. Existing contacts and conversations retain their values. Retain these schema objects on restore; rebuild derived search only from the retained contact records. This migration sends nothing and grants no access.

Back up D1 first; apply once after 310_inbox_contact_search.sql, before serving the updated Worker. Additive only: turns on FTS5 secure-delete for the message search index, so a message's deleted or rewritten words (an erased contact's messages) leave the index's storage instead of staying until its segments merge. One configuration row; no rebuild, no existing row or indexed text changes, nothing is read, sent or queued. Words deleted before this migration stay until FTS5 merges their segments. Exports and backups carry the setting with the index.

Back up D1 first; apply after 311_inbox_message_secure_delete.sql and before serving the updated Worker. Adds only the agent-door retired-reference suppression table from Base bb81810f74ae5cbad9cd786ac84ee738306f63de, without changing existing rows or applied migrations. Nothing is sent or replayed. Retain its value-free digests and erasure markers in installation archives so retirement survives restore.

pendingMigrations.buyerSteps: CHANNELS-001/002: add isolated support-channel connections, scoped text threads, delivery claims and contact-erasure fences. Apply after 270 and before the updated Worker serves traffic. Back up D1, R2 and private configuration; apply before the updated Worker serves traffic, without resetting or editing prior migration ledger rows. Configure authorized provider accounts explicitly. Restored connections are disconnected and pending sends are uncertain; opt-out and erasure fences remain. Media, Teams, approved continuation templates and live provider qualification remain pending.

CHANNELS-001: Apply after 271 with D1/R2/private settings backed up. Adds attachment grants and explicit WhatsApp continuation consent without changing existing consent. Temporary attachment grants never export; opt-out stays fenced. Live provider qualification remains required.

CHANNELS-002: Apply after 272 with D1, R2 and private settings backed up. Adds provider-linked teammate identities, explicit channel/company mappings, action receipts and visible edit/delete notices; retains original transcripts until erasure. Link codes and attachment grants never export. Reconnect with verified Slack scopes/Twilio A2P settings; Teams requires a tenant-scoped installed bot. Live provider acceptance remains pending.

CHANNELS-001: Apply after 273 before serving the updated Worker, with D1/R2/private settings backed up. Retains authenticated subscriber consent facts and permanently fences continuation after STOP. Imports deactivate reply and continuation consent; reconnect never replays held replies.

VOICE-001 partial: apply the additive voice tables after 274_channel_consent.sql and before 276_voice_media.sql, before the updated Worker. Back up D1 and private settings. Configure provider credentials again after restore; restored numbers stay disabled and unknown call commands never replay. Voice launch remains held for live provider, emergency-calling and consent qualification.

Apply after 275_voice.sql before the updated Worker. Back up D1. Existing call media expires one day after admission; expired and withdrawn content stays unavailable after restore. Provider copies require separate cleanup. Voice launch remains held for sandbox, emergency routing and consent qualification.

API-001: back up D1 and private settings, then apply after 280_agent_native.sql before serving the updated Worker. Adds managed connector metadata, encrypted Help Scout custody, cursor and webhook digest fences, Zapier binding and identifier-only contact/article event intents. Existing data and services retain their behavior. Reconnect Help Scout after restore; manual pulls stage reviewed imports and never apply them or replay external writes.

OUTCOMES-002: back up D1 and private settings, then apply after 281_managed_connectors.sql before serving the updated Worker. Rebuilds satisfaction responses and history to admit SMS, WhatsApp, Instagram and Messenger while preserving every prior column and row. Existing invitations and consent are unchanged; unknown sends never replay. Messaging surveys require a live native thread and its current consent/window/registration authority; no templates or in-channel rating replies are enabled.

MOBILE-001 server slice: apply after 282_messaging_surveys.sql and before the updated Worker serves traffic. Back up D1/R2 and private settings first. Adds scoped device capabilities, reconnect frontiers, command receipts and opaque link metadata. Existing native sessions and customer history are retained; no native client or provider delivery is enabled. Pair devices through native sign-in after upgrade. See docs/mobile-api.md.

Apply after 283_mobile_devices.sql and any earlier pending migrations before serving the updated Worker. Back up D1 and retain every migration ledger row. Preserves all existing macro drafts and adds opaque versions for direct per-teammate reply drafts in the same native composer slot. Draft persistence never admits a message or delivery.

Apply after 291_native_ticket_scope.sql before serving the updated source; never rename or replace an applied migration. Adds knowledge_categories.requires_entitlement (default 0), knowledge_collection_entitlements for explicit proven-contact grants and provenance, and knowledge_read_receipts for deliberate article request links. Retain collection restrictions and grants in backups. Live read/sign-in receipts do not transfer; restore sanitization removes complete receipt rows. Contact erasure removes grants, receipts and linked events; member erasure retains scoped pseudonymous grant provenance without widening access. The 30-minute receipt validity is not a retention policy. Exact-candidate acceptance remains pending and both knowledge clauses remain partial.

Apply after 292 before nonmember traffic. Adds knowledge_company_entitlements, knowledge_reply_blocks, knowledge_generation_sources, knowledge_source_index, knowledge_shingles, knowledge_index_dirty, knowledge_write_guards, knowledge_canonicalisation_receipts, knowledge_upgrade_reports and knowledge_upgrade_permits. Knowledge owns pinned bytes and complete generation source sets, including uncited sources; other text stores carry references. Existing domains collections become selected collections with no grants; suggested companies require a deliberate Save. Retain grants, pinned bytes, generation provenance and indexes together. Exclude live receipts, completion receipts, write guards and transient upgrade permits from backups, clear restored upgrade completion and re-establish it before disclosure. The candidate must index and canonicalise existing customer-, application- and model-bound text without replaying outbound work. Exact-candidate upgrade, mutation and performance acceptance remain pending; no reset is authorized.

Apply after 293. Adds knowledge_translation_publications to retain published translation bytes after later reviews; unpublished drafts do not become detector sources. Adds publication and dirty-index triggers so website documents are indexed when their dataset becomes published, even if insert markers were previously consumed. Back up retained publication history with its source/index data. This records an unreleased migration, not an executed upgrade or passing acceptance.

Apply after 294. Adds knowledge_article_publications for exact version-pinned article snapshots and knowledge_retired_articles for durable article deletion fences. Captures current and subsequent published versions, seeds known retired IDs from retained provenance/indexes and prevents deleted IDs from being recycled into newly accessible sources. Current publication, lineage and grants still decide visibility; version equality never grants access. Dataset continuations retain their originally issued bytes while the current publication still contains the URL. Main historical snapshots without an exact publication identity cannot be mapped safely and their continuations fail closed. Retain publication snapshots and retired identities in backups and exclude these authoritative stores from generic text canonicalisation. Exact-candidate acceptance remains pending.

Apply after 295. Adds knowledge_upgrade_progress for durable table/row cursors, row counters, dispatch state and leases while existing workspaces are canonicalised in bounded queue steps. Existing incomplete reports remain incomplete until all scoped tables have been exhausted and the source index is ready; report updates preserve unpublishedArticles. Workspaces created after this migration start with a completed empty report, while subsequent writes use the normal knowledge boundary. Exclude upgrade progress and leases from portable and native SQL backups along with completion receipts; a restored installation must scan again before nonmember disclosure. Upgrade execution and exact-candidate acceptance remain pending. The desktop connector caches context and resumes model sessions outside this round's local-agent/** write scope, so desktop model-input revocation remains blocked and is not claimed by these server changes.

Apply after 296. Never-published drafts do not enter the copy-index dirty queue; current and retained published sources still do. Removes only existing draft markers proved to have no retained published corpus or index. No business rows or reference authority are removed. Strict reversal of unused imported articles removes their owned history/index only after checking all native and generation dependencies; observed source incarnation is checked atomically at new reference and tool-source admission. Ordinary deletion continues retaining retired identity and published history.

Apply after 298 and before serving the updated Worker. Back up D1 and retain all migration ledger rows. Rebuilds operator ticket commands preserving existing rows, primary and unique keys, and the contact-erasure trigger; adds consent-thread links and SMS/WhatsApp kinds. No consent is granted; no provider send is replayed.

Apply after 299 and before serving the updated Worker. Back up D1 first. Creates only new tables for personal Slack notices: administrator consent, each teammate's verified Slack link, per-kind preferences and delivery outcomes; no existing table changes. Personal Slack stays off until an owner or admin enables it on one existing bot-mode Slack connection and each teammate links their own Slack member and opts in per kind. Nothing is backfilled, no consent is granted by the upgrade, and no uncertain send is replayed. These tables are never exported.

Back up D1 and R2 first. Apply once after 300_teammate_slack.sql and before serving the updated Worker. Existing Move in imports stay intact. Business grants remain closed until a Business-provisioned first owner claim with RER_IMPORT_DOOR=on opens the door; ordinary self-host does not set it.

Back up D1 and R2 first. Apply once after 301_import_door.sql and before serving the updated Worker. Adds a source column to Move in runs (existing runs stay uploads) and new tables for the Zendesk OAuth connection, its single-use authorizations, pulls, staged source records (including replies on already imported tickets), refusals, pulled batches and a hash of each pulled ticket's own fields. Tokens and verifiers are stored only as ciphertext under INTEGRATION_ENCRYPTION_KEY; keep that key with the deployment, since a restored connection without it must be reconnected. No connection or pull starts by migration, and Zendesk is never contacted until an owner or admin connects. The Knowledge import's Zendesk API-token path is removed: unset ZENDESK_EMAIL and ZENDESK_TOKEN, and import Zendesk articles through Move in.

Back up D1 first; apply once after 312_agent_door_retired_refs.sql, before serving the updated Worker. Additive only: derived inbox tables (inbox_entries, inbox_tallies, inbox_field_tallies, inbox_tag_tallies, inbox_unread) with their indexes, an index of snooze schedules by conversation and one of contacts by name, and triggers that keep the derived tables current from messages, notes, merges, conversations, AI rows and profiles, snooze schedules, imported-message sources, tag and company links, reads and memberships. The migration fills them once from the existing rows; no existing row changes and nothing is sent, queued or enabled. Every value is derived: each import or restore rebuilds them from the restored rows.

Back up D1 first; apply once after 313_inbox_entries.sql, before serving the updated Worker. Adds the derived table inbox_visitor_waiting (each conversation where a visitor has written since its assistant last did; imported history never counts) with its triggers, and re-creates the inbox entry triggers of 313 so that, in a workspace whose AI replies are draft or off, a waiting visitor's conversation is listed and counted in the team's normal views as one without an assistant. The migration fills the table once from the existing rows and re-derives only the inbox entries it releases; no source row changes and nothing is sent, queued or enabled. Workspaces in auto see no change. Every value is derived: each import rebuilds it from the restored rows.

Back up D1 first; apply once after 314_inbox_visitor_waiting.sql, before serving the updated Worker. Additive only: two small lease tables, contact_erasure_leases (one row per contact while an erasure of that contact runs or was interrupted; ids and an expiry only) and legacy_delta_leases (one row per workspace while a legacy delta package is applied). No existing row changes and nothing is sent, queued or enabled. A lease row left by an interrupted erasure is completed by sending the erasure again; restore keeps the rows so an interrupted erasure stays pending for legacy deltas.
